pr_title: Adding warnings to make generic and static ctor
pr_body:
The trimmer already has intrinsic to analyze annotations for generic types in `MakeGenericType/Method` and warns if a type is not statically known. Adding the matched `RequiresUnreferencedCodeAttribute `to `MakeGenericType/Method` in Type and `MethodInfo ` in the runtime library and propagated the warnings in the library code. 

Suppressed the warning on `DispatchProxyGenerator `since its trim-safe. The existing trimmer behavior does not change for known input types with this change. Also added `RequiresUnreferencedCodeAttribute ` to the `RunClassConstructor `since the trimmer cannot guarantee existence of a static ctor.

Fixes #53121

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/56628 should be the last change needed to fix this. I went through all the intrinsics in linker and they're all annotated (except those in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/56628).

review_comments: I added some support in the linker for validation of array parameters specifically to enable analyzing `MakeGenericType` effectively for arrays with known types passed in and a known `this` value. Why is this being marked as `[RequiresUnreferencedCode]` now?
With this annotation, C#/WinRT effectively becomes untrimmable because there will be `[RequiresUnreferencedCode]` warnings everywhere.

The linker cannot fully reason about annotations on generic argument types and hence the warnings. Regarding C#/WinRT trimming, are there any reasonable workarounds like suppressing the warnings in an easy way?

The linker can reason about the annotations on the generic arguments. I specifically tested that when I did the array work.

For C#/WinRT, it could suppress the warnings, but then it would need to manually propagate the annotations, which is difficult when the linker tooling doesn't help (or actively makes the problem worse, which this will).
I added the support for recognizing the reflection pattern in https://github.com/mono/linker/pull/1955
See a long discussion on this PR, #55102, on the current linker limitation in .NET6 on open generic analysis

I believe the intention is for this to warn only when someone tries to access `MakeGenericType` via reflection since they could invoke it with unknown inputs that we can't validate. We should double-check that the annotation doesn't cause warnings when it's called with known inputs.

The attribute annotations are "the worst case" - linker is free to not warn if it knows better (same for analyzers and so on). In this case the annotation is there for cases where we don't have intrinsic handling. Some of these are in the linker, but any other tool might be in the same position. We have to basically "play it safe".
As long as the linker/analyzer won't warn in cases where all of the inputs are known and can be statically analyzed, then I'll be happy.
